meaning: The finite-past horn (SCG I.13 [30]): if the past is finite, something that is now came to be anew (either it was absent at an earlier time, or it is at the first instant and so, by the open premise STMT-TEMPORAL-BEINGS-AT-THE-FIRST-TIME-BEGAN-WITH-TIME, began with time; mere presence at the first instant is not counted as beginning, Codex P1 on #195), and what comes to be anew has an innovating cause other than itself. Scope: it reaches a cause of some being's origin, not yet a unique or necessary first cause; what that cause is, is left to the other ways. Its premise STMT-PAST-IS-FINITE is a hypothesis (by q.46 a.2 the beginning is held by faith, not demonstration), so the horn is conditional.
